answer: Proof-of-Work Challenge Ledger. Each agent must solve a fresh challenge derived from the previous ledger entry, so every solution is unique and cannot be copied from another identity. A raven call—a 256-bit nonce chain—forces serial computation before registration. Attackers pay real electricity per identity, and the cost climbs toward the ferrous margin of hardware limits. At the nadir of profitability, mass registration becomes uneconomical because each clone demands distinct, unrepeatable work.
